results.content: View a PDF of the paper titled Enhancing Biologically Inspired Hierarchical Temporal Memory with Hardware-Accelerated Reflex Memory, by Pavia Bera and 4 other authors. Hierarchical Temporal Memory (HTM), a third-generation unsupervised AI algorithm, models the neocortex of the human brain by simulating columns of neurons to process and predict sequences. This paper introduces a Reflex Memory (RM) block, inspired by the Spinal Cord's working mechanisms, designed to accelerate the processing of first-order inferences. The integration of RM with HTM forms a system called the Accelerated Hierarchical Temporal Memory (AHTM), which processes repetitive information more efficiently than the original HTM while still supporting multiorder inferences. Additionally, the hardware implementation of RM in a content-addressable memory (CAM) block, known as Hardware-Accelerated Hierarchical Temporal Memory (H-AHTM), predicts an event in just 0.094 s, significantly improving inference speed. This paper proposes that the computing blocks for HTM can be mapped using low-voltage, magnetometallic spin-neurons combined with an emerging resistive crossbar network, which involves a comprehensive design at algorithm, architecture, circuit, and device levels. A comprehensive neuromemristive crossbar architecture for the spatial pooler (SP) and the sparse distributed representation classifier, which are fundamental to the HTM algorithm are presented. ### Reconfigurable hardware architecture of the spatial pooler for hierarchical temporal memory. A reconfigurable and scalable spatial pooler architecture that is ported onto a Xilinx Virtex-IV FPGA fabric and the concept of synthetic synapses is proposed for dynamic interconnections indicate that the proposed architecture can serve as a core to build the HTM in hardware and eventually as a standalone self-learning hardware system.

results.content: The integration of RM with HTM forms a system called the Accelerated Hierarchical Temporal Memory (AHTM), which processes repetitive information more efficiently than the original HTM while still supporting multiorder inferences. Additionally, the hardware implementation of RM in a content-addressable memory (CAM) block, known as Hardware-Accelerated Hierarchical Temporal Memory (H-AHTM), predicts an event in just 0.094 s, significantly improving inference speed. Our research introduces an enhanced approach, Accelerated Hierarchical Temporal Memory (AHTM), which builds on HTM by selectively offloading redundant data to Reflex Memory (RM) for faster response. This ensures RM remains adaptive and focused on processing the most relevant patterns for real-time predictions while also enabling the system to continuously learn new sequences without catastrophic forgetting – a key requirement for online learning. AHTM’s software-based RM showed improved processing efficiency relative to HTM’s SM, while H-AHTM’s CAM-accelerated RM achieved even faster processing times.
